subject: Production flip: safety window, responsibilities, and smoke sprint for NorthStar private deployment
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Tara Singh <tara.singh@northstar-health.com>, Paul Turner <paul.turner@northstar-health.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production flip: safety window, responsibilities, and smoke sprint for NorthStar private deployment

Hi Tara / Paul —

Per our runbook rehearsal last week, we propose the production flip ("safety window") on Friday 2027-04-23 between 02:00-04:00 PT. Goal is a minimal-impact flip with a focused smoke sprint for 60 minutes post-flip to validate key telemetry and L7 functionality.

Quick summary of asks for confirmation:
- Final approval of proposed window (02:00-04:00 PT on 4/23)
- On-call contact list (primary and secondary) for NorthStar infra during the window
- Any additional compliance evidence you want captured during the smoke sprint (e.g., packet captures, audit log snapshots)

Attached is the latest runbook (ns-deploy-runbook-v2.pdf) and a one-page network checklist (network-checklist.csv). I've also included a smoke-results-template.xlsx that Hannah will use to collect pass/fail markers.

Responsibilities (proposed):
- Redwood runtime ops (Karthik): orchestrate model switch, monitor KV cache priming, and validate GPU allocation metrics.
- Redwood platform (Monica): overall bridge lead and escalation path.
- NorthStar infra (Paul): BGP/fabric confirmation and firewall rule application.
- NorthStar app (Tara): user-facing health checks and synthetic transactions.

If the window works, I'll circulate a minute-by-minute plan and escalate list. If you prefer a different time slot, tell us by EOD tomorrow so we can adjust.

Thanks —
Monica
Monica Patel | Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0211

Attachments: ns-deploy-runbook-v2.pdf (pdf), network-checklist.csv (csv), smoke-results-template.xlsx (xlsx)

Monica —

Thanks for the clear plan. 02:00-04:00 PT on 4/23 works for us. Confirming on-call:
- Primary: Tara Singh (me) — +1 415-555-9876
- Secondary: Paul Turner — +1 415-555-9987

For compliance: we need audit log snapshots at T+15 and T+60. Packet captures only if we see connectivity regressions. Please ensure timestamps are UTC in logs.

Also, small ask: can you include a quick checklist item that validates our internal NATS/queue depth after traffic ramp? If the smoke sprint template can capture that metric, that would be ideal.

I'll confirm with our security team if they want any additional artifact collection, but the above should be a good starting point.

—Tara

All —

Couple of operational clarifications from the runtime side:
- We'll perform a staged KV cache priming: canary shard for 5 mins, then parallel priming across remaining shards. Expect an initial spike in GPU utilization (~20-30%) for ~7 minutes.
- We'll enable prefix caching for recurrent prefixes; that stays in the runbook (step 3.2).
- For the smoke sprint, the minimum validations we need from NorthStar are: 3 synthetic L7 requests (success + latency), backend write/reads (DB ping), and NATS queue depth under 1000.

I'll own instrumentation checks + a quick script to snapshot audit logs (UTC) at T+15/T+60. Will post links to logs in the bridge channel as they arrive.

I'll also attach the small smoke-check helper script to the runbook before the window.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Runtime Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: Paul Turner <paul.turner@northstar-health.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Tara Singh <tara.singh@northstar-health.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production flip: safety window, responsibilities, and smoke sprint for NorthStar private deployment

Monica / Karthik —

Confirmed on our side. A couple of notes from infra:
- We'll pre-stage the BGP updates 30 minutes prior and hold them in a pending state; actual withdrawal will be at T0 per your runbook.
- Firewall rules: we pushed the rule set to our edge and the change is queued for the window.
- We'll run a connectivity sweep at T-10 and circulate an IP reachability matrix.

We have one ask: if any downstream vendor calls fail during the sprint, we want an immediate rollback checkpoint at T+20 rather than waiting 60. Can we add an automated fallback at T+20 if the vendor error rate > 5%?

—Paul

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Tara Singh <tara.singh@northstar-health.com>, Paul Turner <paul.turner@northstar-health.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-20T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production flip: safety window, responsibilities, and smoke sprint for NorthStar private deployment

Paul / Tara —

Good catch on the T+20 rollback checkpoint. We'll add an automated rollback trigger if any of these conditions are hit during the smoke sprint:
- vendor error rate > 5% (5xx on external calls)
- NATS queue depth > 2500
- average 95th P50 latency regression > 150% over baseline

Hannah will own the smoke-results document and the T+15/T+60 audit snapshots. Marissa, can you please confirm that CS (customer success) is lined up to notify the account team and coordinate customer comms in the event of rollback?

I'll assemble a minute-by-minute run-of-show and post to the bridge channel (links in related_links). Final artifact to be uploaded to the Drive link by EOD.

Thanks —
Monica

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Tara Singh <tara.singh@northstar-health.com>
Cc: Paul Turner <paul.turner@northstar-health.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-21T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-flip readout: smoke sprint summary and artifacts (NorthStar)

Team —

This is the post-deployment summary from the safety window earlier today (4/23 02:00-04:00 PT). Short version: production flip completed, smoke sprint executed for 60 minutes, and the deployment is green with one transient vendor error that triggered the T+20 checkpoint and was rolled back automatically for 15 minutes while vendors mitigated.

Key artifacts (attached and uploaded):
- smoke-results-template.xlsx (filled) — final pass/fail markers and timestamps
- audit snapshots: audit-20270423-T15.log, audit-20270423-T60.log (UTC timestamps inside)
- network-checklist.csv (final)

Summary of telemetry:
- KV priming: canary shard did 5 min warm, then parallel priming completed in 9 min total; GPU spike peaked at 28% above baseline for 7 minutes and normalized.
- L7 synthetic checks: 5/5 success; p95 latency within SLO (220ms p95 vs baseline 200ms).
- NATS depth: peaked at 1,100 then drained under 600 within 6 minutes.
- Vendor errors: a downstream vendor returned 503 for ~90 seconds at T+18 causing an automatic rollback at T+20; rollback lasted 15 minutes and system returned to green with no data loss and audit logs intact.

Next steps:
- Hannah to share the filled smoke-results spreadsheet and the audit logs to the Drive link and attach to the Jira ticket (JIRA-OPS-1127).
- Schedule a short 30-min postmortem if NorthStar wants a deeper dive on the vendor incident.

Thanks everyone for tight coordination. Closing the safety window as successful.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Customer Success, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
